publications.title: Continuous data assimilation in steady Navier-Stokes equations with unknown viscosity: robust and efficient solvers and fast parameter recovery
publications.summary: This work develops continuous-data-assimilation solvers that recover an unknown viscosity in the steady Navier–Stokes equations from partial flow observations, with quadratic convergence and strong numerical performance even from poor initial guesses.

publications.title: Generalized aliasing explains double descent and informs model design
publications.summary: This work separates prediction error into model insufficiency, data insufficiency, and generalized aliasing, providing an explanation for double descent and practical guidance for model and experimental design.

publications.title: Embracing Uncertainty in “Small Data” Problems: Estimating Earthquakes From Historical Anecdotes
publications.summary: Bayesian inference and uncertainty analysis are used to reconstruct historical Indonesian earthquakes from anecdotal tsunami evidence and assess which conclusions remain robust under explicit modeling assumptions.
publications.venue: Journal of Geophysical Research Machine Learning and Computation
publications.citation: Journal of Geophysical Research Machine Learning and Computation, 2(3), (2025)

publications.title: Model discovery on the fly using continuous data assimilation
publications.summary: Continuous data assimilation turns online model discovery into a finite-dimensional optimization problem, allowing multiple unknown parameters to be updated as observations arrive.

publications.title: Error propagation of direct pressure gradient integration and a Helmholtz–Hodge decomposition-based pressure field reconstruction method for image velocimetry
publications.summary: This work compares direct pressure-gradient integration with a Helmholtz–Hodge reconstruction method to characterize how measurement errors propagate into pressure fields recovered from image velocimetry.

publications.title: Relaxation-based schemes for on-the-fly parameter estimation in dissipative dynamical systems
publications.summary: Relaxation least-squares and Newton schemes provide a general framework for recovering unknown states and parameters together in dissipative dynamical systems.
